subject.title: [Feature]: Support dynamic per-request headers for remote MCP servers

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic per-request MCP header resolver, or should dynamic remote MCP auth/routing stay limited to narrower OAuth, SecretRef, dynamic-env, and caller-context surfaces?
rationale: The code can support a new hook, but choosing the permanent config/API shape changes a security-sensitive remote MCP boundary and overlaps several open narrower proposals.

options.title: Keep umbrella, decide narrow contracts first
options.body: Leave this issue open as the broad design umbrella while maintainers settle OAuth, SecretRef, env-substitution, and caller-context boundaries before approving a generic resolver.

options.title: Approve a generic resolver
options.body: Sponsor a typed opt-in per-server resolver with URL scoping, redirect/redaction rules, docs, and regression coverage across streamable HTTP and SSE.

options.title: Close as covered by narrow work
options.body: Close only if maintainers decide OAuth, dynamic env substitution, SecretRef, and caller-context injection are the supported answers and no arbitrary header hook should exist.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella, decide narrow contracts first
recommendation.body: Leave this issue open as the broad design umbrella while maintainers settle OAuth, SecretRef, env-substitution, and caller-context boundaries before approving a generic resolver.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent MCP operator workflow commits make this the best available routing owner for the product/API decision.
